questions.question_text: A Wyoming salesperson posts a property listing on social media using only her personal name. What violation has occurred?
questions.correct_answer: A blind ad without broker identification
distractors: Failure to obtain a social media license
questions.explanation: W.S. 33-28-119(g) bars a salesperson from advertising real estate without including the real estate company name under which she is licensed, and WREC Rules Ch. 6 Section 4 applies that requirement to every advertisement 'displayed digitally or in print' — social media included. A post carrying only her personal name is a blind ad. Note that a trade name or team name never substitutes for the company name; Ch. 6 Section 4(a) requires the licensed company name to appear concurrently with it.

questions.question_text: A licensee creates an online listing for a vacant lot but never obtained the owner's permission. Which rule was violated?
distractors: Failing to include the property address
Listing vacant land without a survey
questions.explanation: W.S. 33-28-111(a)(viii) makes it a ground for discipline to offer real estate for sale or lease 'without the knowledge and consent of the owner or his authorized agent, or on terms other than those authorized by the owner.' That applies to print, internet, and social media alike. A related ground, 33-28-111(a)(vii), separately requires the owner's written consent before placing a sign on the property.

questions.question_text: Which name must appear in all Wyoming real estate advertisements?
questions.correct_answer: The real estate company name as licensed by the Commission
distractors: A registered trade name or team name by itself
questions.explanation: W.S. 33-28-119(f) and (g) require every advertisement to include the real estate company name under which the licensee is licensed by the Commission, and WREC Rules Ch. 6 Section 4(a) requires that licensed company name to appear conspicuously and concurrently with any registered trade name, group name, or team name. A trade name or team name alone is not enough. Wyoming does not require a license number in advertising; if a licensee uses his individual name, Ch. 6 Section 4(b) requires the legal name in which he is licensed.

questions.question_text: A broker uses a catchy slogan as the only identifier on a billboard promoting residential listings. Is this compliant with Wyoming advertising rules?
questions.correct_answer: No, the licensed real estate company name is required
distractors: Yes, slogans satisfy the identification rule
Yes, if the broker's phone number is included
No, billboards are prohibited for licensees
questions.explanation: W.S. 33-28-119(a) requires a licensee promoting his real estate activities to use the real estate company name under which he is licensed, and to use no slogan or phraseology suggesting the property is offered by an unlicensed private party. Billboards are expressly covered as an advertising medium under 33-28-119(c), and WREC Rules Ch. 6 Section 4(a) requires the licensed company name to appear conspicuously alongside any trade, group, or team name. A slogan by itself leaves the ad blind.

questions.question_text: A WREC investigator reviews a brokerage's Instagram account and finds posts listing homes with only the salesperson's photo and phone number. What enforcement action is most likely?
questions.correct_answer: An administrative fine and/or censure for the advertising violation
distractors: Immediate license revocation of the agent
A warning with no further action required
questions.explanation: WREC Rules Ch. 6 Section 4 applies the advertising identification requirements to all ads 'displayed digitally or in print,' so social media posts must carry the licensed real estate company name (W.S. 33-28-119(g)). Posts showing only the salesperson's photo and phone number are blind ads. Under W.S. 33-28-111(a) the Commission may impose an administrative fine of up to $2,500 per offense, censure, probation, suspension, or revocation — often combined with required advertising-compliance education.

questions.question_text: A salesperson leaves Broker A to join Broker B. Under Wyoming law, who must notify the Real Estate Commission?
questions.correct_answer: The salesperson, and Broker A upon the termination
distractors: Both Broker A and Broker B, but not the salesperson
questions.explanation: W.S. 33-28-109(c) splits the duty: the former responsible broker must immediately notify the Commission for cancellation of the licensee's license upon termination of the association, and the salesperson himself must notify the Commission promptly in writing of the change and pay the required fee. The Commission then issues a new license under the new broker. The new broker has no notification duty — he signs the Commission's transfer form to certify he will actively supervise the licensee. No associate broker or salesperson may associate with a new responsible broker until the new license has been issued.

questions.question_text: A salesperson is terminated by her broker on March 1 but does not affiliate with a new broker. What is the status of her license?
questions.correct_answer: She cannot practice; the license is held, then goes inactive
distractors: It remains active for 90 days after termination
It converts to a broker license
questions.explanation: Under W.S. 33-28-109(c) the former responsible broker must immediately notify the Commission for cancellation of the license upon termination. WREC Rules Ch. 1 Section 5 then controls: a returned license may be held on a 'hold for transfer' basis for not more than thirty (30) days, after which it automatically becomes inactive. From the moment the license is returned, and while it is on hold or inactive, the licensee 'shall not perform any real estate activity.'

questions.question_text: A brokerage opens a second office location in Sheridan. What must the broker do regarding WREC?
questions.correct_answer: Register the branch office with WREC
distractors: Hire a branch manager with 5 years experience
File a new business entity application
questions.explanation: Under W.S. 33-28-109(b) a company license is issued to the responsible broker for each branch office he maintains, and the broker must submit a branch office application plus a plan of supervision for the branch office for the Commission's approval. The branch must use the same trade or business name as the licensed company and remains under the direction and supervision of the responsible broker — no separate broker license and no independently qualified branch manager is required.

questions.question_text: A salesperson whose license is inactive due to broker termination shows a property to a buyer. What is the consequence?
distractors: No violation if a sale is not completed
questions.explanation: WREC Rules Ch. 1 Section 5(e) bars a licensee on inactive status from engaging in any real estate activity, and Ch. 6 Section 1(a)(ii) makes 'participating in real estate activity while a license is on inactive status' an express ground for discipline. Showing a property is real estate activity. The Commission may impose an administrative fine of up to $2,500 per offense under W.S. 33-28-111(a), along with censure, probation, suspension, or revocation.

questions.question_text: Broker A terminates a salesperson but fails to notify WREC. Meanwhile, the salesperson closes a transaction under Broker B. Who bears regulatory liability?
questions.correct_answer: Both brokers may face WREC discipline
distractors: Only Broker A for failing to notify
No liability if the transaction was proper
questions.explanation: Broker A violated W.S. 33-28-109(c), which requires the responsible broker to immediately notify the Commission for cancellation of the license upon termination of the association. Broker B has no notification duty, but 33-28-109(c) bars a salesperson from associating with a new responsible broker until the new license has been issued, and 33-28-111(a)(ix) makes failure to supervise an affiliated licensee a ground for discipline. WREC Rules Ch. 6 Section 1(a) expressly allows action against a licensee and/or that licensee's responsible broker, so both brokers are exposed.

questions.question_text: In Wyoming, who is ultimately accountable for the real estate activities of affiliated licensees?
questions.explanation: Wyoming law makes the responsible broker accountable for all real estate activities conducted by affiliated licensees. This includes ensuring compliance with WREC rules, maintaining trust accounts, and keeping proper transaction records.

questions.question_text: A salesperson mishandles earnest money by depositing it into a personal account. Besides the salesperson, who else may face discipline?
questions.explanation: The responsible broker is accountable for trust account management and all real estate activities of affiliated licensees. Even if the salesperson acted independently, the broker's supervisory duty makes them subject to WREC discipline for the trust fund violation.

questions.question_text: Which records must a Wyoming responsible broker maintain for WREC examination?
questions.explanation: Wyoming's responsible broker must maintain trust accounts and transaction records and make them available for WREC examination upon request. This recordkeeping requirement supports consumer protection and regulatory oversight of brokerage operations.

questions.question_text: A responsible broker discovers that an affiliated salesperson has been practicing outside the scope of the License Act. What is the broker's obligation?
questions.correct_answer: Take corrective action and ensure compliance
distractors: Wait for WREC to investigate first
Report only if a complaint is filed
questions.explanation: The responsible broker must ensure all affiliated licensees comply with WREC rules and the License Act. Upon discovering a violation, the broker has an affirmative duty to take immediate corrective action rather than waiting for a formal complaint or investigation.

questions.question_text: A brokerage has 15 salespersons and no written supervision policies. During an audit, WREC finds multiple compliance failures across the office. How will WREC likely view the broker's role?
distractors: WREC has no authority over internal policies
The broker is exempt if no complaints existed
questions.explanation: W.S. 33-28-102(b)(xlix) defines the responsible broker as the individual responsible for supervising the activities of the licensees associated with the company, and 33-28-111(a)(ix) makes failure to supervise an express ground for discipline. Widespread compliance failures across a 15-agent office point squarely at inadequate oversight. Wyoming requires a formal written plan of supervision only for branch offices (33-28-109(b)), but the absence of any written policy is strong evidence the supervisory duty was not being met.
